gri_path: GRI 1: candidate headings are 8408.10 (marine propulsion diesel engines), 8407.21/.29 (spark-ignition marine engines), 8483.40 (gearing/drive units, e.g. stern or Z-drives), 8501 (electric propulsion motors) and 8487.10 (ship propellers)

Section XVI note 3: a composite unit (engine + reduction gear + shaft/propeller) is classified by its principal function, the power source supplying propulsion -> marine propulsion engine; assumed diesel
GRI 6: 8408.10.00 marine propulsion engines; ship-scale output assumed to exceed 746 kW -> .50

rejected_alternatives.reason: applies if the unit is a drive/transmission (stern drive, Z-drive, azimuth thruster gear unit) without its own engine, as for the outboard drive in H82350
applies if the unit is an electric propulsion motor/pod
applies only to ship propellers and blades imported alone
spark-ignition marine engines; ship propulsion is normally diesel
power 373-746 kW; ship-scale output assumed higher

missing_facts: What does the propulsion unit consist of (diesel engine, engine with gearbox/shaft/propeller, azimuth or Z-drive thruster without engine, electric pod motor)?
Type of engine (compression-ignition, spark-ignition, electric) and power output in kW
Is it a complete unit or a part of a vessel's propulsion system?
classification.rationale: The description gives only 'a ship propulsion unit', so the heading cannot be fixed. A unit that incorporates its own power plant takes the principal function of propulsion under Section XVI note 3 and would be a marine propulsion engine of 8408.10, most likely above 746 kW for a ship. A drive unit without an engine would instead go to 8483.40 (as the outboard drive in NY H82350, in force), and an electric pod to 8501. The unit's composition and power source must be confirmed.
